sections.h2: What are the quickest ways to sell a house in Johnson City?
sections.html:
The quickest routes in Johnson City are a cash sale to a buyer who accepts the house as is, or a listing priced to move that is ready for showings. A traditional sale adds time for buyer financing, appraisal and repair negotiations, so it suits owners who are not under a deadline.

Johnson City is a college and medical center, and it has a large rental population, so a house can attract an owner-occupant, a landlord or a flipper. That mix is useful when your property needs work.

  • List with an agent when the house shows well and you can wait for financing to clear.
  • Sell directly when you already have a buyer lined up and just need a closing agent.
  • Take a cash offer when you need a firm date or the house needs repairs you do not want to fund.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Johnson City for a home seller?
sections.html:
Johnson City lies in an Appalachian valley at about 1,634 feet, mostly in Washington County with parts in Carter and Sullivan counties. It began in 1856 as Johnson's Depot, a railroad station, and was incorporated in 1869. Three rail lines crossed downtown, including the Clinchfield Railroad and the narrow gauge line nicknamed Tweetsie.

Today it is a medical and education center. East Tennessee State University has about 16,000 students, and Ballad Health, the region's largest health system, is headquartered here. Johnson City Medical Center includes a Level 1 trauma center and Niswonger Children's Hospital. The Mountain Home veterans campus, authorized by Congress in 1901, sits across from the university.

Buffalo Mountain, a ridge over 2,700 feet, is a city park on the south side, and the Watauga River arm of Boone Lake touches the city limits. Most of the city is in the Johnson City Independent School District, with Science Hill High School, Indian Trail Middle School and Liberty Bell Middle School, while small parts of the city fall in the Washington County school district. Verify the district for a specific address before you advertise a school zone.

The climate is humid subtropical, with about 45 inches of precipitation and 15.6 inches of snow a year.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Johnson City housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 74,943 residents for July 1, 2025, a 5.5 percent rise from the April 2020 base. The city has 30,662 households, and 42.5 percent of adults aged 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $268,200
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 51.3 percent
  • Median gross rent: $1,023
  • Median household income: $57,254
  • Mean commute: 18.7 minutes

With about half of homes rented and a university in town, expect buyers to include landlords. That can raise interest in a duplex or a house near campus.

sections.h2: What drives Johnson City housing demand?
sections.html:
Health care and the university set the pace. Wikipedia describes a Med-Tech corridor anchored by Johnson City Medical Center, Franklin Woods Community Hospital, and the East Tennessee State University medical and pharmacy colleges. The metro area's gross metropolitan product was reported at $9.1 billion for 2019.

The Census Bureau's 2022 business tallies point the same direction: $2.10 billion in health care and social assistance receipts and $2.96 billion in retail sales, or $40,793 per resident. Johnson City Transit runs 11 fixed routes and carried 386,917 trips in 2025, and Tri-Cities Regional Airport in Blountville provides air service. Buyers who work at the hospital or campus usually search near those routes, so mention bus access or commute time when you describe the house.

sections.h2: How is property tax billed and paid in Johnson City?
sections.html:
Johnson City collects its own city property tax, and Washington County's Trustee collects the county tax. For 2026, city notices were mailed the week of October 12, and the bill is due by February 28, 2027. Penalty and interest begin to build on March 1, 2027.

You can pay in person at the Municipal and Safety Building, 601 E. Main Street, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., by mail to P.O. Box 2227, or online with a 2.75 percent processing fee. For questions, call the tax office at 423-434-6299.

The county side works the same way. Washington County's Trustee mails notices in October, payable through the end of February, and adds 1.5 percent interest on balances left on March 1. The county's page lists a 2023 county rate of $2.15 per $100 of assessed value and notes that city residents owe more on top. By state law the official tax roll is set as of January 1, and the county says taxes are normally prorated at closing with the buyer made the responsible party.

sections.h2: What does the recording and transfer step cost in Washington County?
sections.html:
Deeds for most Johnson City houses are recorded at the Washington County Register of Deeds in the historic courthouse at 100 E. Main Street in Jonesborough. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., stops recording at 4 p.m., and answers at 423-753-1644. The register collects the state transfer and mortgage taxes along with recording charges.

The transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of price, so a sale at the Census median value of $268,200 would produce about $992 in tax. The county also runs a free Property Fraud Alert that emails you when a document is filed under your name.

Because Johnson City stretches into Sullivan and Carter counties, confirm which county holds your parcel. Look at the tax bill or call the register's office before you assume where the deed will be filed.

sections.h2: What permits and rental taxes matter to Johnson City sellers and buyers?
sections.html:
The city's Building Division requires permits for most construction work and runs them through the CityView portal or the permit counter in City Hall. A single-family owner who lives in the home may act as their own general contractor, and may do their own electrical or plumbing work after passing a free competency exam. Mechanical work must go to a licensed mechanical contractor. Call 423-434-6047 with questions, including inspection requests.

Short-term rentals are taxed locally. Every stay under 30 days, whether booked online or directly, is subject to the city's 7 percent Hotel/Motel Transient Occupancy Privilege Tax, and continuous stays of 90 days or more are exempt. Operators must also collect state and local sales tax, and the total depends on which county holds the property.

County portion of Johnson CityTotal lodging tax rate
Washington County16.5%

Source: Johnson City Finance Department occupancy tax page. Call the city's tax specialist at 423-232-1480 for lodging questions.

sections.h2: Which repairs and inspections should I plan before listing?
sections.html:
Johnson City's building staff publishes a guide to common residential inspection fails, and it is a good checklist before you list. Under the city's reading of the 2012 International Residential Code, a deck is exempt from a permit only if it is no larger than 200 square feet, no more than 30 inches above grade, detached from the house and not serving a required exit door. Prefabricated pools under 24 inches deep are also exempt.

Anything beyond that, including additions, decks attached to the house and covered porches, needs a site drawing and a permit. Inspection requests received by 4:30 p.m. may be scheduled as early as the next business day. A buyer paying cash may take a house with open items, while a buyer using a loan may ask for them to be resolved before closing.

faqs.q: When are Johnson City property taxes due for 2026?
faqs.a: February 28, 2027. The city mailed notices the week of October 12, 2026, and penalty and interest start on March 1, 2027. Call 423-434-6299 with questions.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for a Johnson City house?
faqs.a: In Washington County it goes to the Register of Deeds at 100 E. Main Street, Jonesborough, 423-753-1644, which stops recording at 4 p.m. Parcels in the Sullivan or Carter County parts of the city fall under those counties' registers.

faqs.q: Can an owner pull their own permits in Johnson City?
faqs.a: An owner who occupies a single-family home may act as general contractor. Electrical or plumbing work also needs the owner to pass a free competency exam at the Building Division, and mechanical work needs a licensed contractor.

faqs.q: What tax applies to a short-term rental in Johnson City?
faqs.a: Stays under 30 days carry the city's 7 percent occupancy tax, plus state and local sales tax. Total lodging tax is 16.5 percent in the Washington County portion of the city.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a Johnson City sale?
faqs.a: The state charges $0.37 per $100 of purchase price, so a $268,200 sale carries about $992 in transfer tax. The contract decides whether the buyer or seller pays.
